lines: Magistrate Greaves: Order. Order! Thank you. The Ash Assize is in session. It is always in session. Sessions are billed by the hour.
Magistrate Greaves: You want a verdict on the Ruskweber wage plates? Then you need the jury. Five jurors, out walking the heath. Win each one over.
Magistrate Greaves: By 'win over' I mean beat in a duel. This is Ashmere. Persuasion is a contact sport.
Magistrate Greaves: Five votes for you. Unanimous! The court is moved. Deeply. Financially, even.
Magistrate Greaves: And now the verdict, which I wrote last Tuesday.
Magistrate Greaves: Not all five votes yet? The jury walks the heath. Like the dead, but with lunch breaks.

greaves_after: Magistrate Greaves: Court is adjourned. Court is always adjourned for you now. Permanently. Mind the step.
verdict_caught: You lay Clerk Tansy's docket on the bench: 'Verdict: for the clan (prepaid). Jury: advisory.' Dated last Tuesday.
Magistrate Greaves: ...Advisory means they advise and I ignore. It's a very old tradition. Fine. Take the clan's bribe, then. Somebody should enjoy it.
verdict_struck: Magistrate Greaves: Guilty! Of wasting the court's time. And of trespass, loitering, and having the wrong friends. Bailiffs?
Magistrate Greaves: The jury? Advisory, dear. They advise. I decide. Read the docket next time. Nobody reads the docket.
bailiffs_defeat: Bailiff: Sentence served, I suppose. Here, court costs. Refunded. Don't tell the magistrate.
bailiffs_lose: The bailiffs throw you out onto the heath. The heath does not catch you.
ledger_verdict: Greaves let you win all five jurors of the Ash Assize, then read out a verdict the clan had paid for the week before.

lines: Clerk Tansy: The docket is on my desk. Page two. I'm not telling you to read it. I'm telling you where it is. Those are different crimes.
Clerk Tansy: I write down what the court says. Sometimes before it says it. Saves ink.
Clerk Tansy: I've started a second docket. The true one. It's very short and very rude.
Briony Cask: They say I stole a wage plate from the gravers' hall. Me! I can't even lift a wage plate. I've tried. Often.
Briony Cask: Tell the magistrate I was with you on the heath that night. One little oath. Friends swear for friends. We're friends now. Aren't we?

briony_after: Briony Cask: No hard feelings. Feelings are for people who own things. I own a lot of things now. Some of them were yours.
briony_betray: Your oath gets Briony off. Outside, she hands the wage plate to two Ruskweber fences, then points at you.
Briony Cask: That one swore in court they were with me. Under oath. Which makes them my accomplice. Get them.
briony_reward: Briony walks free and keeps her word, which surprises both of you. She slips you a tonic from the evidence locker.
briony_kept: Your oath is not needed. The magistrate loses the file. Briony thanks you anyway, and counts her fingers after the handshake. Yours too.
fence_defeat: Ruskweber Fence: Accomplice, she said. Accomplice my foot. You're a witness, and witnesses get paid to forget.
fence_lose: The fences take your coins as 'evidence'. Evidence is never returned.
ledger_alibi: Briony Cask asked you to swear she was with you on the heath, then used the oath to call you her accomplice.

lines: Mourner Mercer: Professional grief. Weeping by the hour, wailing by arrangement, fainting on request. I do a lovely faint.
Mourner Mercer: Business is booming. Three funerals tomorrow. Pin these notices on the three boards of the heath, would you? My knees are in mourning.
Mourner Mercer: All three pinned. Wonderful. Old Abner Tull, the widow Grice and young Pell the slag-picker. Tragic. Sudden. Tomorrow.
Mourner Mercer: Don't visit the departed, by the way. It upsets them.
Mourner Mercer: Three boards, three notices. Pin them straight. Nobody trusts a crooked funeral.
Mourner Mercer: I'm rehearsing. Sob, sob, wail. Sob, wail, faint. The faint goes last. Always leave them wanting more.
Mourner Mercer: You found the auction book. Rude. Yes, I bury them first and sell the house after. The families get a lovely service. And the bill.
Mourner Mercer: Old Tull would have died eventually. I just got the paperwork in early. Now, shall I mourn you? I'll give you the family rate.

mercer_defeat: Mourner Mercer: Beaten by the guest of honour. Fine. I'll cancel the funerals. Do you know what a refund does to a mourner's soul?
mercer_lose: Mourner Mercer: There, there. Sob. That one was free.
mercer_after: Mourner Mercer: I do weddings now. Same tears, better cake, and the bride only wishes she were dead.

lines: Old Abner Tull: My funeral? Tomorrow? I've not even finished my soup.
Old Abner Tull: Mercer did the widow Grice last spring. She was out picking berries. Came home to a buyer measuring her curtains.
Old Abner Tull: He keeps an auction book in the Bellows Deep, where nobody looks. Go and look.
Old Abner Tull: I walk the heath every day to show the clan I'm still breathing. It's the only exercise that pays.
Old Abner Tull: Still alive! I've ordered a cake to celebrate. Mercer's baking it. I'm having it tasted first.
Tally Keeper Orla: I kept the tag board of the Bellows Deep. You hang your tag when you go down, you take it back when you come up.
Tally Keeper Orla: The clan shut the Deep eleven years ago. Eight tags never came back to my board. Find them for me. A board with holes in it looks careless.
Tally Keeper Orla: Four tags lie out on the heath, they say. The other four went down with the shift.
Tally Keeper Orla: All eight. Hamm, Odo, Gage, Bert, Tuck, Rosa, Molly, Penn. That's the whole last shift.
Tally Keeper Orla: Strange. The tags from the Deep are new brass. Somebody has been stamping fresh ones. You don't stamp tags for the dead. Take these, I don't need leaves.
Tally Keeper Orla: Fresh tags means a live shift. Go down to the bottom gallery of the Deep. If I'm wrong, bring back nothing. Nothing is easy to carry.
Tally Keeper Orla: Alive? Digging? For eleven years? And Slagg signs for their wages every month?
Tally Keeper Orla: I stamped those tags myself, you know. I'll stamp one for Slagg too. For when he goes down and doesn't come up.
Tally Keeper Orla: Slagg's at the bottom of his Deep. Fitting. Go and give him the news.
Tally Keeper Orla: Eight tags on the board. Eight. First time in eleven years my board's been full. I cried. Don't tell the clan, they'd charge for it.
Painter Corwin: I paint the wild Spirlings of the heath. Portraits. Very lifelike. Some of them have complained.
Painter Corwin: Bring me eight kinds in your team to sit for me. Four from the heath, four from the Deep. A wealthy patron has ordered the whole set.
Painter Corwin: The set is sold! To Magistrate Greaves, for the court archive. Art in a courthouse. Isn't that hopeful?
Painter Corwin: A Brickwarden! Chin up. No, its other chin.
Painter Corwin: A Peatbloom! Chin up. No, its other chin.
Painter Corwin: A Bellowroc! Chin up. No, its other chin.
Painter Corwin: A Charsylvan! Chin up. No, its other chin.
Painter Corwin: A Fumeregent! Chin up. No, its other chin.
Painter Corwin: A Lodemarshal! Chin up. No, its other chin.
Painter Corwin: A Vitrillaxe! Chin up. No, its other chin.
Painter Corwin: A Clinkerdome! Chin up. No, its other chin.
Painter Corwin: Eight! The set is done. Every kind, every scale, and where it nests, down to the stone. My patron insisted on the stones. Here, for your trouble.

corwin_more: Painter Corwin: Still missing some. The heath kinds are shy, the Deep kinds are shy and bite. Art is suffering. Mostly yours.

lines: Painter Corwin: Deeds? My portraits are deeds? Greaves stamps each one and the clan owns the kind? And catching one is theft?
Painter Corwin: ...I may have known. A little. Here are my sketches, the originals. Without them the court can't prove a thing. What do we do with them?

choices.action: quest_stage ah_deeds 2; set_flag ah_deeds_burned; give_item kin_charm 1
quest_stage ah_deeds 2; set_flag ah_deeds_sold; give_item tide_pearl 1; battle deed_hunters

deeds_burned: The sketches curl up in the spring fire. Corwin watches his best work go up and paints you instead, badly, as thanks.
deeds_sold: Greaves pays in a confiscated pearl and stamps the deeds on the spot. Your own Spirlings are now Ruskweber property, and the catch tax collectors were waiting outside.

lines: Painter Corwin: I've gone back to landscapes. Nobody can own a landscape. Well. The clan owns this one. But it doesn't know.
Painter Corwin: My portrait of you sells well. Under WANTED. I'm sorry. I'm also very well paid.

hunters_defeat: Catch Tax Collector: Tax paid in full. In bruises. We'll accept that, this once.
hunters_lose: The collectors stamp your hand with the Ruskweber mark. It washes off. The shame doesn't.

lines: Usher Pim: The court keeps a bench for witnesses to rest on. Witnesses rest a lot here. Some of them permanently.
Usher Pim: Your Spirlings look tired. Let them rest. No charge. The charge comes later.
Supplier Rook-Hale: Tonics and brews, sold at the court's fixed prices. Fixed as in arranged.
trader.action: shop strong_tonic max_tonic remedy revival_leaf cooling_gel dash_brew guard_brew power_brew

lines: Juno: Rookie! Fancy meeting you down here. Slagg's payroll chest is at the bottom. Big enough for two.
Juno: Partners. I take the left gallery, you take the right. Meet at the chest. Trust me, I've changed. Rivals are so last act.

split_caught: You remember the note from the first gallery: 'J. - right gallery, bring the net. S.' You take the left gallery.
Juno: ...You read my mail? That's low. That's beautiful. Fine. No net, no partners. Just you and me, the old way.
split_struck: The right gallery ends in a net and three of Slagg's pit hands. Juno's voice drifts down from the left: 'Sorry, rookie! Slagg pays per head!'
net_defeat: Pit Hand: Out of the net? Juno said you'd be easy. Juno says a lot of things. Juno owes us money.
net_lose: The pit hands haul you up in the net and dump you on the heath. Juno waves from a safe distance.
ledger_split: Juno Sallow offered to split Slagg's payroll with you in the Bellows Deep and sent you down the gallery where his net was waiting.

lines: Overman Slagg: Visitors! In a closed mine! Officially, you're not here. Officially, nobody is. Officially, I'm a widower with a small pension.
Overman Slagg: The shift digs, the clan pays their wages, I collect the wages. Everyone gets something. The shift gets exercise.

slagg_defeat: Overman Slagg: All right, all right! I'll tell them the mine closed. I'll even say sorry. In writing. Unsigned.
Overman Slagg: Take the payroll key. Eleven years of wages. Some of it is even still there.
slagg_lose: Overman Slagg: Clocked out. Come back when you've learned to dig.
slagg_after: Overman Slagg: I'm digging now. Eleven years of my shift to make up. The shift says I'm doing it wrong. The shift is enjoying this.

lines: Shift Boss Hamm: Closed? The Deep? Nobody told us. We've been digging for eleven years.
Shift Boss Hamm: Slagg brings bread on Sundays and takes our wage slips on Mondays. Says the clan pays in arrears. Very long arrears.
Shift Boss Hamm: Tell Orla we're alive. She'll want her tags back. She was always strict about tags.
Shift Boss Hamm: Mind the props. They're older than you and less forgiving.
Shift Boss Hamm: Eleven years of back pay! We're going up tomorrow. First thing I'll do is look at the sky. Second thing, sue.
